faq.subheading: Here's what people usually ask before using TrainMitra.

items.q: Is TrainMitra affiliated with IRCTC or Indian Railways?
items.a: No. TrainMitra is an independent, community-run project. Every delay reason, live update and experience rating comes from real passengers, not an official feed - so for anything booking-critical, always double-check on the official IRCTC site.

items.q: Where does live train status come from if there's no GPS tracking?
items.a: From passengers actually on board. There's no satellite or GPS feed behind it - people post the station (and platform, if they know it) as the train passes through, and it updates in real time for everyone else tracking that same train.

items.q: How does the Tatkal countdown work?
items.a: It's a fixed rule, not a live feed: AC classes open at 10:00 AM and Sleeper/Second Sitting at 11:00 AM, one day before the journey, from the train's origin station. TrainMitra just calculates the next opening time and counts down to it. It assumes the train runs daily, so if a train only runs on specific days, double-check that on IRCTC too.

items.q: What's the difference between Tatkal Experience and Journey Experience?
items.a: Tatkal Experience is about booking - passengers report how many minutes after opening a class actually sold out, so you get a real sense of how fast Tatkal moves for that train. Journey Experience is about the ride itself - ratings for cleanliness, food, staff behaviour, punctuality and safety from people who've actually travelled on it.

items.q: Are delay reports and live status updates reset every day?
items.a: Yes, both reset automatically at midnight IST, and the date on a report is always set by our server rather than something you can pick - that stops old or backdated reports from lingering or being used to dodge moderation. Tatkal and Journey Experience aren't reset daily since those are long-running community averages, not day-specific reports.

items.q: How are fake or spammy reports kept in check?
items.a: A few ways: everyone gets a daily posting limit, any report that gets heavily downvoted automatically blocks that user from posting again for the rest of the day, and votes are one per person per report. It's not perfect, but it keeps the noise down without needing constant moderation.

items.q: Do I need an account to use TrainMitra?
items.a: Only to post - a delay report, a live update, an experience rating or a vote. Searching for trains and routes, and reading everything the community has already shared, is open to everyone without logging in.
Completely. No ads, no paid tiers, nothing to unlock - it only exists because passengers are willing to share what they see.
